mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 6.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below -1% for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during INDPRO < -1% for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST below their respective 12-month moving averages signals weakening housing and overall demand, which depresses consumer spending and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST fall below their 12-month MAs.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in CPIAUCSL above 3% while FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for three months signals inflation without a corresponding policy response, which erodes real purchasing power and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 3% and FEDFUNDS < 1% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust job growth, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS > 12-month MA for five months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated increase in both GDPC1 and RSAFS above their 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months signals strengthening aggregate demand and corporate cash flows, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-month MA AND RSAFS > 12-month MA for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and RSAFS are above their 12-month MAs for two months.
